groups.title: Irregularity foundation
groups.proposal: Make perfective-stem shape and form-meaning alignment the two main kinds of VNC irregularity.
groups.writingJob: Classify a known irregular VNC by its real paradigm relation while leaving unknown stems to the regular system.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to look first at perfective-stem formation and tense-form meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies stem, subject, mood, and tense; the application recognizes the paradigm relation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Stem, Subject, Mood, and Tense; no irregularity checkbox.

groups.title: Speech criterion and regular sound change
groups.proposal: Judge irregularity by sound and keep regular sound changes under their regular Lesson 2 and Lesson 7 rules.
groups.writingJob: Reuse the canonical regular sound-change path when the spoken formation is regular, even if spelling changes.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader avoid calling a form irregular merely because its spelling looks different.
groups.decisionSplit: The application decides whether a sound operation is regular; the user does not classify it.

groups.title: Rare perfective-stem irregularities
groups.proposal: Apply compound class shifts and conditioned t-to-h perfectives, exposing only Canvas-authorized alternatives.
groups.writingJob: Generate the correct irregular perfective stem by compound class and participant-tense conditions, and allow an authorized alternative where Canvas permits one.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the rare class-shift and t-versus-h perfective patterns.
groups.decisionSplit: The user may select between authorized results; the application determines when the choice exists and enforces every condition.
groups.controlPolicy: Show one Irregular Result picker only for a cell with more than one authorized result.

groups.title: Form-meaning dislocation
groups.proposal: Separate a verb's tense meaning from the tense form used to express it.
groups.writingJob: Map semantic present and general past to the authorized morphological tense and block forbidden forms.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recognize preterit-as-present and distant-past-as-past patterns.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended time meaning; the application chooses the required form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Tense as meaning; do not ask the user to choose the hidden morphological tense.

groups.title: Standing, lying, and hanging
groups.proposal: Generate the positional verbs through their authorized tense relations and fused locative structure.
groups.writingJob: Build ih-ca, on-o, and pil-ca with their preterit-as-present and distant-past behavior and the conditioned on fusion.
groups.readingJob: Guide the positional reading and its form-meaning contrast.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the stem and meaning; the application supplies form and fusion.

groups.title: Defective ā
groups.proposal: Keep ā defective and generate its present or absent interpretation through polarity.
groups.writingJob: Allow only the authorized preterit-shaped paradigm and apply the conditioned negative allomorph.
groups.readingJob: Guide present-versus-absent readings of the same defective family.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses polarity and participant; the application enforces defectiveness.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Polarity and Subject; no defectiveness control.

groups.title: Itzi, hui-tz, and carrying compounds
groups.proposal: Keep motion itzi defective, generate hui-tz and its carrying compounds, and distinguish homophonous alert itz.
groups.writingJob: Enforce the compound-only motion stem, delete post-stem k where required, and apply the authorized present, past, command, and lexical-reading conditions.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the motion compounds and the distinct alert or observant homophone.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended reading only for ambiguous itz; the application builds or blocks the form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Reading only when itz is ambiguous; no control for automatic stem operations.

groups.title: Defective am-i-h constructions
groups.proposal: Generate defective am-i-h only with its required quēn constructions, including incorporated quēn.
groups.writingJob: Require an authorized quēn construction, build the preterit-as-present VNC, and keep sentence particles outside the VNC unless quēn is incorporated.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through interrogative, evaluative, negative, and traditional solid spellings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the genuine construction; the application enforces defectiveness and placement.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the existing Construction picker; no separate defectiveness control.

groups.title: Zero-root existence, mani, and nemi
groups.proposal: Preserve the zero root of Ø-i-h, require pronominal NNC cooperation, and apply mani and nemi's exact lexical tense and referent relations.
groups.writingJob: Build only the authorized zero-root cooperative form, keep mani's preterit on mani, select man or nen where required, and mark mani's referent usage.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through homophonous amihqueh structures and the meanings and uses of mani and nemi.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the construction and, for mani, may state the referent kind; the application performs the structural and tense work.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Construction and add one contextual Referent picker shown only for mani.

groups.title: Being and existence suppletion
groups.proposal: Generate the ye, ca-t, and ca-h members from one being and existence paradigm.
groups.writingJob: Select ye, ca-t, or ca-h by mood, tense, number, and locative context, including the marked antiquated ca-t form only when chosen.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through suppletion, antiquated catqui forms, contextual meanings, and traditional spellings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses mood, tense, subject, direction, and an authorized marked variant; the application selects every ordinary stem member and ending.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Tense, Subject, Directional, Polarity, and the existing marked-alternative picker; no paradigm-member picker.

groups.title: Going suppletion
groups.proposal: Generate yā, ya-uh, hui, and yah from one going paradigm.
groups.writingJob: Select the correct going stem by mood, tense, and subject number, delete forbidden post-hui k, and block singular cen-hui and dispreferred dialectal forms.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through the shared paradigm, spelling ambiguities, dialectal forms, and the archaic ya-hui compound analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses mood, tense, and subject; the application selects the stem and applies its boundary rules.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Tense, and Subject; no paradigm-member or dialect picker.

groups.title: Coming with fused huāl
groups.proposal: Build the coming paradigm by fusing huāl to the appropriate member of the going paradigm.
groups.writingJob: Select the going member, fuse huāl, apply l plus y assimilation, and prevent a second directional prefix.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recognizing all fused members as one coming paradigm and its traditional dictionary name.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses mood, tense, and subject; the application selects and fuses the correct member.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Tense, and Subject; no Directional or paradigm-member picker for fused huāl.

groups.title: Irregular idioms
groups.proposal: Keep idiomatic lexical meaning separate from productive paradigm formation.
groups.writingJob: Apply an idiomatic reading only when its complete authorized construction is present.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to the whole-construction meaning rather than a word-by-word false reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the construction; the application recognizes its authorized idiomatic reading.
groups.controlPolicy: No idiom checkbox; recognition is automatic.
